summary:
MARS EXPLORER is an interactive web platform that transforms NASA's Martian datasets into an accessible environment for exploring the Red Planet, understanding its terrain, and planning simulated astronaut missions.

The platform combines real Mars rover imagery, scientific map layers, geographical discovery, and route-planning tools into one unified interface. Users can explore actual Martian locations, investigate their geological characteristics, and understand how terrain conditions could influence future human exploration.
details:
MARS EXPLORER — Project Description

MARS EXPLORER is an interactive planetary exploration experience that combines education, entertainment, and scientific discovery to make exploring the Red Planet accessible and engaging. Inspired by popular geographical discovery games such as GeoGuessr, our project takes the concept of identifying locations from visual clues and brings it beyond Earth — onto the surface of Mars.

The platform allows users to explore Mars through interactive 3D visualisations, real planetary imagery, and geographical discovery challenges. In its exploration game mode, players are presented with views of the Martian surface and must use visual clues such as terrain formations, rocks, craters, and surrounding landscapes to estimate where the location is on a map of Mars. The closer their guess is to the actual location, the higher their score. This creates an entertaining challenge while naturally encouraging players to observe and learn about Martian geography.

Beyond the game itself, MARS EXPLORER features an interactive 3D globe with discoverable geographical landmarks. Users can select points of interest to learn about significant Martian features, including volcanoes, craters, and other geological formations. Each discovery provides educational information and relevant imagery, helping users understand the planet beyond its appearance.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our primary goal is to make planetary science more approachable, particularly for students and people who may not usually engage with scientific datasets. Rather than presenting information through traditional educational material alone, we use game mechanics, exploration, and visual interaction to encourage curiosity and active learning.

The project aims to:

  • Make Martian geography and planetary science more engaging and accessible.
  • Encourage users to recognise geological formations and understand the diversity of the Martian landscape.
  • Introduce users to real imagery and scientific information collected through space exploration missions.
  • Create an interactive learning experience that combines entertainment with meaningful educational value.
  • Demonstrate how geographical visualisation and scientific datasets can be transformed into accessible digital experiences.

Tools and Technologies

MARS EXPLORER was developed as a web-based application using modern frontend technologies. Our development stack includes React and TypeScript for the application structure and functionality, Vite as the development and build tool, and Tailwind CSS for styling and interface design. Interactive geographical visualisations and planetary imagery form the foundation of the experience, supported by publicly available NASA and planetary science resources.

We also incorporate authentic planetary imagery, including material credited to NASA, JPL-Caltech, ASU, and MSSS, to help ground the experience in actual space exploration data.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of MARS EXPLORER lies in applying a familiar gaming concept to an entirely different world. GeoGuessr demonstrates how identifying locations through visual observation can be entertaining and educational. We adapted that principle for Mars, where players must interpret unfamiliar landscapes instead of recognising familiar cities, roads, and landmarks.

We also wanted to go beyond a conventional quiz or informational website. The interactive 3D Mars globe, discoverable landmarks, immersive surface imagery, and competitive scoring make the platform feel like an exploration experience rather than a digital textbook.

By combining game design with real planetary science, we aim to create an experience where users learn not because they are required to, but because they are curious to discover what lies beyond the next location.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors when developing the project:

  • Scientific authenticity: We wanted the experience to be grounded in real Martian imagery and credible scientific information rather than entirely fictional environments.
  • Educational value: Gameplay needed to encourage observation and geographical understanding, not simply reward random guessing.
  • Accessibility: The interface needed to be intuitive enough for casual players while still offering interesting information for space enthusiasts.
  • Engagement: We incorporated scoring, rounds, interactive locations, and exploration mechanics to encourage users to keep discovering.
  • Visual experience: We aimed for an immersive, space-inspired interface that reflects the scale and atmosphere of planetary exploration.
  • Feasibility: Given the development constraints of a hackathon, we prioritised a functional and engaging core experience while leaving room for more advanced scientific visualisation and mission-planning capabilities in future development.

Ultimately, MARS EXPLORER aims to turn the exploration of another planet into something people can actively experience. It brings together the curiosity of gaming and the value of scientific discovery, allowing anyone to take a virtual journey across Mars and learn something new along the way.
